headline: Bridgeport rally backs police chief as union calls for his removal
dek: About 60 residents, clergy, elected officials and retired officers rallied for Chief Roderick Porter as union complaints and an outside review keep pressure on Bridgeport’s police leadership.
body: A public split over Bridgeport’s police leadership widened over the weekend when residents, faith leaders, elected officials and retired officers rallied in support of Police Chief Roderick Porter. The Oct. 3 gathering outside the city’s Government Center drew about 60 people, according to the [Connecticut Post](https://www.ctpost.com/news/article/bridgeport-leaders-rally-for-chief-roderick-porter-22461046.php), while members of the police union continue to call for Porter’s removal.

The rally was organized by former Bridgeport detective Harold Dimbo and City Council member Mary McBride-Lee. Speakers described Porter as accessible and engaged with neighborhoods, and several supporters said his presence in the community has built trust. The [CT Mirror](https://ctmirror.org/2026/10/05/bridgeport-ct-police-chief-roderick-porter-rally/) reported that residents and retired officers also framed the event as a defense of reforms that have shaped the department’s relationship with Black officers and the wider community.

The show of support does not resolve the complaints from inside the department. AFSCME Local 1159 President Michael Salemme told the Connecticut Post that union leaders view the rally as a small political event and continue to point to complaints and lawsuits involving Porter. The CT Mirror reported that Salemme cited more than 20 complaints filed by officers with the state Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities, along with several federal lawsuits. Those allegations have not been adjudicated by the rally or by the news reports, and they should not be treated as findings of misconduct.

The central dispute is now moving on two tracks. Union representatives have sought an investigation into Porter’s leadership and working conditions, while Mayor Joe Ganim has agreed to hire an outside investigator but has declined to remove the chief. The Connecticut Post reported that Ganim has continued to support Porter, citing the department’s public-safety record, even as critics press for a change in command. Neither the mayor nor the union has announced a final result from the review.

Porter did not attend Saturday’s event, but he told the CT Mirror he appreciated the community support and connected it to relationships built during his career and tenure as chief. He became a Bridgeport officer in 1993 and was appointed chief in 2022, according to the Connecticut Post. The rally also highlighted an internal divide among members and former members of the Bridgeport Guardians, a minority-officer organization: some current union-aligned critics have opposed Porter, while retired Guardian members at the event defended him.

That divide matters because Bridgeport’s police department is both a public-safety agency and one of the city’s most visible institutions. Questions about working conditions, discrimination claims, overtime management and leadership accountability can affect morale inside the force, public confidence outside it and the city’s exposure to legal costs. But the available reporting does not establish that any one side’s account is complete, and the size of Saturday’s rally cannot measure the views of the city as a whole.

The next meaningful test will be the outside review and any public response from the mayor, union and police department. Until that process produces findings, the confirmed facts are narrower: supporters rallied for Porter, union leaders continue to seek his removal, and Bridgeport’s administration has chosen an investigation over an immediate change in command. Residents and officers are therefore watching the same unresolved question from opposite sides—whether the chief’s record represents needed reform or a workplace crisis that requires new leadership.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoTitle: Bridgeport rally backs Police Chief Roderick Porter
seoDescription: Bridgeport residents and retired officers rallied for Police Chief Roderick Porter as a police-union dispute and outside review continue.
